title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Admitting an Application — Goods, Booking and Quantities
content:
## Clause

An application under Dangerous Goods Acceptance is admitted into the category that corresponds to the goods as declared, and only if the goods, the booking and the quantities all fit that category. Admission tests rest on the line's own records of the booking and of the application; they are taken on the application date.

## Admission checklist

1. **Booking type and state.** The booking that will carry the goods shows dangerous goods as its cargo type and is live, which for this purpose means its status is requested, confirmed or equipment released.
2. **Hazard classification.** The declared IMDG class is on the category's list of classes and the declared packing group is on its list of packing groups. Goods that would come within a category solely by being packed as limited quantities are placed in AHL DG Limited Quantity. A class that no category lists is not carried at all.
3. **Booking particulars.** The container type on the booking is one the category permits, the booking's trade lane is one on which the category is carried, and the booking's port of discharge is not among the ports the category refuses.
4. **Quantities.** The containers applied for do not exceed the category's per-acceptance container ceiling; the declared gross weight does not exceed the per-acceptance weight ceiling; and the gross weight, spread evenly across the containers, does not exceed the per-container weight ceiling.
5. **Contract rating.** Where the category demands a contract-rated booking, the booking is rated under a service contract.

The applicant's own standing — the age of its profile, recent misdeclaration penalties and any waiting period after a rejection — is tested as part of the same admission.

## Effect of admission

An admitted application is registered with the status submitted, together with an initial declaration that awaits the shipper's signature.

## Worked quantity check (hypothetical ceilings)

The ceilings in this example are invented. Take an application for 3 containers and 51000 kg, under a category whose per-acceptance ceilings are 4 containers and 60000 kg and whose per-container ceiling is 16000 kg. The container count and the total weight pass. Spread evenly, the weight is 17000 kg per container, which is above 16000 kg, so the quantity test fails. The same weight on 4 containers gives 12750 kg each and passes.

## Points of judgement

**A booking already gated in — does it count as live for admission?** No. Only the statuses requested, confirmed and equipment released are live for this test.
